q: A cylinder has radius 6 cm and height 10 cm. A cone has the same radius and height. What is the difference between their volumes? (Use π = 22/7)
exp: Cylinder volume = 360π. Cone volume = 120π. Difference = 240π = 754.29 cm³.

q: A cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is topped by a hemisphere of the same radius. What is the total volume? (Use π = 22/7)
exp: Cylinder volume = 1540 cm³. Hemisphere volume = 2/3×22/7×343 = 718.67 cm³. Total = 2258.67 cm³.

q: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm is topped by a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. Find the combined volume. (Use π = 3.14)
exp: Cylinder = 3.14×9×8 = 226.08 cm³. Hemisphere = 2/3×3.14×27 = 56.52 cm³. Total = 282.60 cm³.

q: A cone has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Find its curved surface area. (Use π = 3.14)
exp: Slant height = √(3²+4²)=5 cm. CSA = πrl = 3.14×3×5 = 47.1 cm².

q: A spherical ball has radius 6 cm. If its radius is doubled, how many times does its volume increase?
exp: Sphere volume is proportional to r³. Doubling the radius increases volume by 2³ = 8 times.

q: If the radius of a cylinder is doubled while its height remains unchanged, its volume becomes how many times the original?
exp: Cylinder volume is proportional to r². Doubling radius makes volume 2² = 4 times.

q: If the height of a cylinder is doubled while its radius remains unchanged, its curved surface area becomes how many times the original?
exp: CSA = 2πrh, so it is directly proportional to height. Doubling height doubles the CSA.

q: The radius of a sphere is increased from 4 cm to 8 cm. What is the ratio of the new volume to the old volume?
exp: Volume is proportional to r³. Ratio = 8³:4³ = 512:64 = 8:1.
